s1.syndrome_frame: A slowly growing eyelid mass with recent changes and crust formation
salient_findings: Yellowish-brown, well-circumscribed papule on the central lower eyelid
Flakier surface at one lateral end
Hyperkeratotic lesion with pseudohorn cysts and neoplastic squamous cell proliferation
key_facts: 4-year history of a left lower eyelid mass
Recent growth and crust formation
Papule is well-circumscribed and located on the central lower eyelid
Tumor has a flakier surface at one lateral end
Specimen measured 0.8 × 0.5 × 0.3 cm
Hyperkeratotic lesion with many pseudohorn cysts
Proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells
Malignant squamous cells have eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli
Mitotic figures are present
Ki67 staining highlights scattered basal cells and approximately 20-40% of tumor cell nuclei

raw.syndrome_frame: A slowly growing eyelid mass with recent changes and crust formation
salient_findings: Yellowish-brown, well-circumscribed papule on the central lower eyelid
Flakier surface at one lateral end
Hyperkeratotic lesion with pseudohorn cysts and neoplastic squamous cell proliferation
key_facts: 4-year history of a left lower eyelid mass
Recent growth and crust formation
Papule is well-circumscribed and located on the central lower eyelid
Tumor has a flakier surface at one lateral end
Specimen measured 0.8 × 0.5 × 0.3 cm
Hyperkeratotic lesion with many pseudohorn cysts
Proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells
Malignant squamous cells have eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli
Mitotic figures are present
Ki67 staining highlights scattered basal cells and approximately 20-40% of tumor cell nuclei

raw.rationale: The presence of malignant squamous cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli, along with mitotic figures and a high Ki67 staining rate, supports the diagnosis of squamous cell carcinoma.

rejected.label: Keratoacanthoma
rejected.why: Although keratoacanthoma can present with a similar hyperkeratotic lesion and pseudohorn cysts, the presence of malignant squamous cells and mitotic figures suggests a more aggressive malignancy like squamous cell carcinoma.

rejected.label: Merkel cell carcinoma
rejected.why: Merkel cell carcinoma typically has a more aggressive clinical course and characteristic neuroendocrine differentiation, which is not described in the histopathological examination.

rejected.label: Syringoid eccrine carcinoma
rejected.why: This tumor type is less common and typically involves the eccrine glands, with a different histological appearance than the one described.

rejected.label: Sebaceous gland carcinoma
rejected.why: The histopathological findings do not support sebaceous gland carcinoma, as there is no mention of sebaceous differentiation or characteristic 'foamy' cells.
